key_idea: Erik's move can never be worth more than grandpa's previous one, so he can only tie, and he ties iff grandpa never takes the last window of the current maximum value; each value phase is therefore a normal-play impartial game solved with Sprague-Grundy.
sketch: While the maximum window value is v, both players only take v-windows, and a move clears 4 consecutive cells so it splits a cluster into independent left and right parts. Split the string into clusters at gaps of 3 or more empty cells and compute Grundy numbers with an interval DP per cluster (windows may overhang the interval ends), rebuilding once per phase. Erik moves to nim-sum 0 whenever possible; grandpa is random so he leaves a non-zero nim-sum almost immediately, after which Erik finishes every phase himself, and the 1-phase is even by parity. Sum of L^3 over clusters is small (clusters average ~14 cells), about 0.13 s per game. Pitfalls: clamp overhanging windows into [1, N-3], track the current maximum incrementally, flush each move. The checker cannot judge an interactive problem: samples_passed reflects my own simulator of grandpa (720 full N=1e5 games, all tied exactly) plus a pipe-based grader on small inputs.
